name: Einstein-Rosen Bridge
description: The model of a particle that Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen proposed in 1935: two identical sheets of space joined at a smallest sphere, the bridge. The neutral bridge is Schwarzschild's exterior taken twice and joined at $r = r_s$, and the charged bridge is Reissner and Nordström's metric with the sign of the electric term reversed, which needs no mass.
convention: The Schwarzschild radius is $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, and $r_q$ is the charge radius, which Einstein and Rosen write $\epsilon/\sqrt{2}$. We keep factors of $c$ explicit, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: How do you make a particle in a theory that has only fields? Albert Einstein's answer in the spring of 1935 was that it had better not be a singularity, "for a singularity brings so much arbitrariness into the theory that it actually nullifies its laws" [einstein1935]. Ludwik Silberstein had written to him with a case in point, a static field with two point singularities that sit at rest and never fall toward each other [einstein1935, weinstein2015twobody]. So Einstein and Nathan Rosen, his assistant in Princeton, asked whether matter and electricity could be built from the metric and Maxwell's potentials alone, with no singular point anywhere [einstein1935, weinstein2015twobody]. Their paper was received on 8 May 1935, a week before the paper with Boris Podolsky on whether quantum mechanics is complete was published, and it was printed on 1 July [einstein1935, einstein1935epr].¶Picture Schwarzschild's space as Ludwig Flamm found it in 1916, a funnel that narrows to a smallest circle of radius $r_s$ and stops [flamm1916, lobo2016]. Schwarzschild's $g_{rr}$ is infinite on that circle, and to Einstein and Rosen that made it a singularity [einstein1935]. They traded the radius for a new coordinate, $u^2 = r - r_s$, and let $u$ run over the whole line, so that $r$ comes in from infinity to $r_s$ and goes back out again [einstein1935]. On Flamm's funnel $u$ is the height, $z = 2\sqrt{r_s}\,u$, so negative $u$ is a second funnel hanging upside down under the first and joined to it at the narrowest circle [flamm1916, einstein1935]. They called "such a connection between the two sheets" a "bridge", and the bridge was to be a neutral particle, a neutron or a neutrino [einstein1935]. A negative mass allows no such change of coordinate, which they took as the reason no particle has one [einstein1935].¶The price of the bridge is that $g_{tt}$ vanishes on it, and the determinant of the metric with it, so the field equations, which divide by that determinant, read $0/0$ there [einstein1935]. On a suggestion of W. Mayer, Einstein and Rosen multiplied the equations through by the square of the determinant, and tried the cure first on the field of a uniformly accelerated frame, whose $g_{tt}$ vanishes on a plane in the same way [einstein1935]. Electricity asked for more: a charged bridge exists only if the Maxwell field enters Einstein's equations with its sign reversed, a negative energy density, so that the charge lowers $-g_{tt}$ by $r_q^2/r^2$ and Reissner and Nordström's two horizons become one [einstein1935, lobo2016]. With that sign the mass can be set to zero, and $u^2 = r^2 - r_q^2$ gives a bridge of radius $r_q$ made of charge alone, "an elementary electrical particle without mass" [einstein1935].¶The test of the idea was to be two bridges moving under each other's pull, and Einstein and Rosen left it undone: "one cannot even know whether regular solutions with more than one bridge exist at all" [einstein1935]. Einstein did not find one, and soon gave the bridge up as a model of a particle [weinstein2015twobody]. The geometry lay unused for twenty years, until John Wheeler threaded electric lines of force through a tunnel in space in 1955, so that each mouth looks like a charge with no charge anywhere, and with Charles Misner in 1957 named the tunnel a wormhole [wheeler1955, misner1957, lobo2016]. Could a signal take the tunnel and beat light going the long way round? Following Schwarzschild's bridge through time in Martin Kruskal's coordinates, Robert Fuller and Wheeler found in 1962 that the throat "pinches off in a finite time and traps the signal in a region of infinite curvature" [kruskal1960, fuller1962].¶In Kruskal's coordinates the two sheets are the two outside regions of the extended Schwarzschild spacetime and the smallest circle is the horizon, where $g_{tt} = 0$ means that light sent toward the bridge takes infinite $t$ to arrive [kruskal1960, lobo2016]. In the extension the two sheets touch on a single sphere, and in the chart of $t$ and $u$ they meet along the whole hypersurface $u = 0$ [guendelman2009]. For Eduardo Guendelman, Alexander Kaganovich, Emil Nissimov, and Svetlana Pacheva, writing in 2009, the difference is matter: the metric written in $u$ fails the vacuum equations on that hypersurface, since $\sqrt{-g_{tt}}$ goes as $|u|$, whose second derivative is a delta function, the mark of a shell of lightlike matter lying on the bridge [guendelman2009]. A bridge that a traveller could cross came from Michael Morris and Kip Thorne in 1988, who kept the two sheets and the throat, removed the horizon, and paid with matter whose tension exceeds its energy density [morris1988].¶Did the two papers of 1935, the bridge and the paradox, have anything to do with each other? In 2013 Juan Maldacena and Leonard Susskind proposed that they are one thing: "the Einstein Rosen bridge between two black holes is created by EPR-like correlations between the microstates of the two black holes", which they called the ER = EPR relation [maldacena2013]. Two black holes joined by a bridge are then two black holes maximally entangled, and Fuller and Wheeler's pinch matches a property of entanglement, since neither the bridge nor the entanglement can be used to send a signal [maldacena2013, fuller1962]. They went further and speculated "that even the simple singlet state of two spins is connected by a (very quantum) bridge of this type" [maldacena2013]. The bridge can even be propped open: when Ping Gao, Daniel Jafferis, and Aron Wall coupled the two sides of such a pair in 2017, a signal got through, by a route they related to quantum teleportation [gao2017].

related.text: Each sheet of the neutral bridge is Schwarzschild's exterior, and the bridge is his horizon. Martin Kruskal's extension holds both sheets, with a black hole and a white hole between them [kruskal1960].

The charged black hole, whose electric field has positive energy. The charged bridge is its metric continued to $r_q^2 \to -r_q^2$, the Maxwell stress tensor entering Einstein's equations with the opposite sign [einstein1935].

The bridge propped open by one number. Thibault Damour and Sergey Solodukhin added $\lambda^2$ to $-g_{tt}$, so that clocks on the throat still tick and light crosses it, and at $\lambda = 0$ their metric in $t$ and $u$ is the neutral bridge [damour2007].
The wormhole made to be crossed. Michael Morris and Kip Thorne kept the two sheets and the throat, removed the horizon, and paid with matter whose tension exceeds its energy density [morris1988].

A moment of the charged bridge with no mass is a moment of Ellis and Bronnikov's wormhole, $du^2 + (u^2 + r_q^2)d\Omega^2$ with $r_q$ for their $\ell$. Their $g_{tt}$ is $-1$ everywhere, so their throat has no horizon [ellis1973, bronnikov1973].
The other spacetime that carries the two names. Einstein and Rosen found the cylindrical gravitational waves again in 1937, two years after the bridge [einstein1937].

A slice of space with two bridges in it, each leading to a sheet of its own, which Dieter Brill and Richard Lindquist wrote down in 1963 [brill1963]. Charles Misner's slice of 1960 joins the two mouths to each other and makes a wormhole within one sheet [misner1960].
The bridge with one of its sheets closed off by a universe of dust. Wheeler's bag of gold is reached by passing through the bridge [marolf2009].
A closed universe of $N$ masses whose moment of greatest expansion has a bridge at every mass, each opening onto a sheet of its own [clifton2012].

Hoffmann's particle of the same year, a point charge of Born and Infeld's electrodynamics whose whole mass is the energy of its field. Einstein and Rosen pointed out to him the conical point left at its centre [hoffmann1935, tahvildarzadeh2011].
The bridge folded in half. Misner and Wheeler made each point of one sheet the same as the opposite point of the other, which leaves one sheet and a bridge that leads back into it [misner1957].
B I continued through $r = b$ is a bridge of the same kind, two asymptotically flat regions joined at a neck [hruska2019].

coordinates.name: Einstein-Rosen

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the neutral bridge

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $u^2 = r - r_s$ for the areal radius $r$, so $u$ is the square root of a length, positive on one sheet and negative on the other. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.

coordinates.convention: We use Schwarzschild's coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ on one sheet, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.

coordinates.name: Isotropic
domains: r \to 0 \;\text{(the far end of the other sheet)}

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the neutral bridge

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the isotropic radius, so the areal radius is $r(1 + r_s/4r)^2$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{2048r^4\,r_s\left(4r - r_s\right)}{\left(4r + r_s\right)^7}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{2r_s}{r\left(4r + r_s\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(4r - r_s\right)}{4r + r_s}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(4r - r_s\right)\sin^2\theta}{4r + r_s}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Charged, Areal Radius

parameters.description: Schwarzschild radius, $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, the areal radius of the neutral bridge
Charge radius, $r_q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for a charge $Q$, the areal radius of the massless charged bridge

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$ on one sheet, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $r$ the areal radius, and the bridge is the sphere $r_+ = \left(r_s + \sqrt{r_s^2 + 4r_q^2}\right)/2$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} + \dfrac{\left(r\,r_s + 2r_q^2\right)\left(r^2 - r\,r_s - r_q^2\right)}{2r^5}\dot{t}^2 - \dfrac{r\,r_s + 2r_q^2}{2r\left(r^2 - r\,r_s - r_q^2\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r^2 - r\,r_s - r_q^2}{r}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{\left(r^2 - r\,r_s - r_q^2\right)\sin^2\theta}{r}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

parameters.description: Charge radius, $r_q^2 = GQ^2/(4\pi\epsilon_0c^4)$ for a charge $Q$, the areal radius of the massless charged bridge

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, u, \theta, \phi)$ for the bridge with no mass, $r_s = 0$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and $u^2 = r^2 - r_q^2$ for the areal radius $r$, so $u$ is a length, positive on one sheet and negative on the other. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter $s$, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/ds$.
